newsitem.title: USA: Mass. moves to cut welfare benefits after 2 years.
newsitem.headline: Mass. moves to cut welfare benefits after 2 years.

text.p: Massachusetts has sent the federal government a plan to let the state put into effect a new two-year limit on welfare benefits, as it tries to further cut the number of people in the program.

Since February 1995, the state had been seeking to put the new time limit into effect. But the Clinton Administration had not granted it the waiver that was needed to shut off Aid to Familes with Dependent Children to able-bodied recipients two years after the youngest child in a family turns age two.
The new federal reforms to the welfare system pave the way for Massachusetts to put all its new rules into effect.
"Now we can really put some bite in the idea that benefits are not infinitely extendable," said Gov. William Weld, in prepared remarks that were released on Monday.

Many of the reforms Massachusetts wanted already are in place, including a work requirement for able-bodied people with schoolage children after 60 days, and a rule barring cash benefits to recipients who have more children.
Further, teen parents must live with their families or in a structured, supervised setting, and these parents are required to finish high school or obtain equivalency degrees.
Such stiff new rules have cut the state's welfare caseload by almost 20 percent to 82,751 cases, the lowest level in more than 23 years, since they went into effect in February 1995.
